newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Assa Abloy to change listing to avoid tax.
newsitem.headline: Assa Abloy to change listing to avoid tax.

text.p: Swedish lock maker Assa Abloy AB said on Wednesday its would apply for a listing on the smaller O list of the Stockholm Stock Exchange to avoid a new wealth tax.
Assa Abloy said in a statement its board had decided to apply for the listing from July 21, 1997.
"The reason is the changed wealth tax in Sweden," Assa Abloy finance director Goran Jansson told Reuters.

The company joins a group of Swedish companies which have decided to de-list their shares from the bourse's main A list to avoid a tax of 1.5 percent on 100 percent of the value of shares listed on the A list.
Shares on the smaller O list remain exempt from the tax.
The group includes fashion retailer Hennes & Mauritz, media group Marieberg AB, construction group Lundbergs and investment companies Latour and Custos.
"Several shareholders brought up the issue and we could not see any good reason to stay on the A list, causing more taxes to be paid by Swedish shareholders," Jansson said.
Large shareholders had no objection, he added.
